title: Finite colimits under closed-immersion algebra direct image
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $g:(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to(Y,i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ be the canonical ringed-space map [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. Then the functor $g_*$ on all module sheaves [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] preserves finite colimits. No quasi-coherence, complex, rank function or derived-category hypothesis is imposed.

source.document: Stacks Project, Sheaves on Spaces and Sheaves of Modules
source.place: Tags 00AE (Lemma 6.32.1) and 01AX (Lemma 17.6.1); direct-image-algebra map of Tag 0AVW; parent reconstruction proof step 1

proof.text: On the closed image, cofinal inverse-image neighborhoods identify direct-image stalks with source stalks. On its open complement direct-image stalks vanish. Since g has the identity map on its pushed-forward ring sheaf, these are identifications of the corresponding modules, not merely of sets.

Short exact sequences of module sheaves are detected on stalks, so g_* is exact. It is additive and hence, as an exact functor between abelian categories, preserves finite colimits. The empty source gives the zero functor and causes no exception.
